mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST drops by more than 5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and confidence decline.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS shows a sustained increase over three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 8% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a strong labor market recovery, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity accelerates.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 8% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE > 8% and PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals an inflationary environment with accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic outlook deteriorate.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where GDPC1 decreases by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter.
